content.text:
Headless flows: `--provider copilot --model <id>` with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` (OAuth or fine-grained PAT), or a saved entry's key slot (`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>`). `/provider export cicd [auth]` exports the CURRENT provider for CI/CD — the full JSON (config + embedded secret) or, with `auth`, the bare secret value for the secrets store; `/provider export` + `/provider import` move the current provider between machines via a passphrase-encrypted clipboard container (secrets never print to the transcript).

## CLI flags

CLI: `/provider chatgpt oauth [headless]` (callback server in `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server.dart`, exported from `lib/io.dart`). `/provider codemie` asks for the org URL first (Enter applies the hosted default, issue #1809), then SSO vs JWT; `/provider codemie sso [orgUrl]` (callback server in `lib/src/cli/codemie_sso_server.dart`, exported from `lib/io.dart`) and `/provider codemie jwt [orgUrl] [token]` skip the prompt. Headless: `--provider dial --model <deployment> [--base-url …]` (dial has no default model id — `buildCliDefaultModel` throws without `--model`).

## Roles × custom providers

A `roles:` chain entry can name a saved `customProviders:` entry **by name** (issue #1552) — the natural hand-written config works instead of silently degrading to a single model:

```yaml
customProviders:
  - name: aiai
    apiType: openai          # the adapter dialect (catalog spec)
    baseUrl: https://api.bycom.by/v1
    modelId: glm-4.6
    keyName: AIAI_API_KEY    # optional: the env/secure-store slot for the key

roles:
  default:
    - provider: aiai         # names the entry above
      model: glm-4.6
```

Rules:

- **Kind-vs-name**: resolution order is catalog name, then adapter kind (`chatgpt-codex`), then the `customProviders:` registry. Registry entries can never be named after catalog providers (reserved names), so the two namespaces never shadow. An entry known to NEITHER catalog nor registry still skips + degrades exactly as before (the roles config falls back to the single model with one warning — which also prints in the TUI, not only stderr).
- **Defaults**: the entry supplies `baseUrl` and `keyName` where the chain ref omits them; explicit ref fields always win.
- **Key slots** (issue #40 precedence): a custom endpoint's key resolves
  from the entry's pinned `keyName` first, then the endpoint-scoped
  `FA_KEY_<HOST>` store slot (e.g. `FA_KEY_API_BYCOM_BY`) or its
  `_2`/`_3`… rotation stack, and only then falls back to the adapter
  dialect's catalog env names (`OPENAI_API_KEY` for an `openai` entry —
  the last-resort fallback, shared with the dialect's default endpoint).
  Export `AIAI_API_KEY=<key>` (or `/key set FA_KEY_API_BYCOM_BY <key>`)
  and every chain entry referencing the entry resolves.

## Scoped provider timeouts (issue #1554)

`connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (strict positive ints, ≤ 1 h) are
valid on three config surfaces: `roles:` chain entries (map form),
`customProviders:` entries, and `models.custom:` entries. Per FIELD, the
first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180 s, idle 300 s)
```

Per-field fallback: an entry overriding only `streamIdleTimeoutMs` leaves the
connect leg at the lower levels. Configs without the keys behave
byte-identically (the standing uncapped-run rule). When a scoped override is
in effect the stall line names it (`idle window 1800s (role default
override)`), so a wide window never reads as a hang.

Slow-local-model recipe: a local endpoint that thinks minutes before the
first byte needs the IDLE leg widened, not the whole config. On the role
chain entry pinning the local endpoint set only `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2×`
its worst silent prefill stretch — every cloud provider in the same config
keeps the global watchdog untouched.

```yaml
roles:
  default:
    - provider: openai
      model: local-thinker
      baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
      streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000   # this entry only
  smol: [openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini]   # keeps 300s
```

content.text:
`dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
===
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh-1537 there are
  NO main CI runs — "tag-only" is literal: tags/dispatch/schedule only.
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
  Flake intake consumes PR-dispatch runs only (gh-1537:
  `scripts/flake_watch.py` filters to `workflow_dispatch` events — the
  retired main trigger leaves SM validation dispatches and v* tag runs;
  a red tag run is a release-flow failure, triaged by daily-publish /
  ci-red-report, never quarantined as a flake). Dedup is per test name
  (the #1364 lesson): one test red across N runs files ONE issue.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs
  pre-merge in ci.yml's `pty-visual` leg — gh-1538 retired the nightly
  duplicate — and on demand).

# gh-2096: [GOAL] auto-compact: judge robustness for slow/unusable judge classes — cross-run health latch, per-call budget token, timeout diagnosis

## Description

> **Correction (sanity check):** an earlier version claimed the judge receives the unbounded full ledger (~125k tokens) and proposed a ledger cap. That was wrong: `ledger.render()` is bounded to the newest **512 entries** (~20k tokens) since #541/#543 (`judgePreviewEntries`, `structured/ledger.dart:91`) — present in the incident build too. The observed every-run timeouts are therefore NOT prompt-size growth (they persisted even after a pass shrank the context by 30%). This card is re-scoped to the defects that remain real; the earlier ~40k static-cap idea (and its derivation comment, now removed) is moot — the cap already exists.

## Problem

The hide judge is a single LM call under a fixed attempt budget (300s default; `compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds` knob from #541). Observed in production: with the smol role on a mandatory-reasoning (forced-thinking) flash-class model behind a coding-plan gateway, **every** judge call hit the full budget — across days and across sessions, large and small (bounded input makes size irrelevant; reasoning time or endpoint queueing dominates). What turns this into a recurring tax:

1. **The retry is born cancelled.** A budget timeout cancels the run-wide `budgetSource` token (`structured/engine.dart` `_callJudge` → `budgetSource.cancel`), and the retry judge call is wired to that same token (`agent/auto_compactor.dart`) — it fails almost instantly (~75 ms in the logs) and only pushes the failure counter toward the deterministic fallback.
2. **Judge-health amnesia.** `_runHidePasses` resets the consecutive-failure counter every run — the full budget is re-paid by EVERY new auto-compact run for as long as the configured class stays slow/unusable.
3. **No honest timeout diagnosis.** The failure line names role/model/budget (#541 AC3) but not the attempt shape (input entries/est. tokens, elapsed, TTFT) — so "slow-reasoning class" vs "wedged/queueing endpoint" is indistinguishable from logs.

## Proposed change

1. **Cross-run judge-health latch** (persisted per session): consecutive failures survive across runs; while latched, auto-compact runs skip the judge (deterministic hide immediately); a cheap periodic probe (or the first small successful call) unlatches.
2. **Per-call budget token**: a child `CancelToken` per judge call — a timeout aborts only the in-flight call; the retry and later LM stages of the run keep a live token.
3. **Timeout diagnosis in the receipt**: the judge failure line records input size (entries + est. tokens) and elapsed — slow-class vs queued-endpoint becomes visible from logs alone.
4. Docs: the model-class requirement for the smol/judge role (a class that can answer within the budget — e.g. non-mandatory-reasoning — or a budget sized to the class). Config-level guidance only; no product names.

## Why it helps

- The budget tax becomes **once per session** (latch) instead of once per run.
- A real retry can succeed (e.g. transient queueing) instead of dying in ~75 ms.
- Operators can distinguish "slow class" from "wedged endpoint" without reproducing.

## Pros

- Model-class-agnostic; composes with existing #541 fallback, #515 budgets, #2044 escalation.
- Small, isolated engine changes; the 512-entry input bound already shipped and stays.

## Cons / risks

- The latch adds session state; a recovered judge stays unused until the probe (bounded by probe cadence).
- On classes where the budget is genuinely unwinnable the judge stops contributing until the class or budget changes — by design; the receipt should say so explicitly ("judge latched: budget unwinnable for the configured class").

## Acceptance

- TDD: fake slow judge → the first run pays the budget once, the next run goes straight to deterministic; the probe unlatches on success; a timeout cancels only the in-flight call (retry and later stages stay live); the receipt contains entries/tokens/elapsed.
- >90% line coverage of new `lib/` code; docs + CHANGELOG.

Prior art: #541/#543 (deterministic fallback, 512-entry input bound, `judgeBudgetSeconds`, named failure line); #515 (budgets); #2044 (escalation).

- **Session survival (owner directive):** every write this card adds is append-only/additive; no migration rewrites or replaces session files; a fixture proves an old (large) session loads unchanged — byte-identical apart from the new additive records.

Priority: **1 of 9** (auto-compact epic).

docs/agents/cli.md:19:Failures fall back to manual entry. `startAgentModelFlow` pins the `smol`/`subagent` role chains through `ModelRolesResolver.setRoleChain`/`clearRoleChain` (the resolver is created on demand when the config had no `roles:` section — `AgentCliConfig.modelRolesResolver` is mutable) and persists via `onModelsConfigChanged` (`bin/fah.dart`'s `persistConfig` reads the live resolver config).

Watchdogs (`provider_common.dart`): `providerConnectTimeout` 60s, `providerStreamIdleTimeout` 120s between bytes — wedged endpoint errors out so the resolver can fail over. Config: `roles:`/`modelOverrides:`/`retry:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` (invalid schema = `ConfigException`). Shared models: `media_model_slots.dart` (shared with app's `MediaModelsStore`) and `models_config.dart` (per-slot media overrides + named custom model definitions `/model <name>` resolves; persisted by host).
docs/agents/project-layout.md:137:- `lib/src/task/` — `task` tool: parallel subagents, batch `{context, tasks[]}` + `background`; children never get `task` (no nesting); `explore`→`smol`, `review`→`slow`; `outputSchema` ONE fix retry; child failure = per-item error. `/tasks` lists jobs, `/tasks cancel <id>`; completions re-enter parent as async-result (`agent://<id>`). Subagents retained: real JSONL child sessions, `task_status`/`task_observe`/`task_send`, child-only `reply` + sibling `agent_message` (pending-queue + hop-capped), `completed_without_reply` notice.

valid on three config surfaces: `roles:` chain entries (map form),
`customProviders:` entries, and `models.custom:` entries. Per FIELD, the
first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180 s, idle 300 s)
```

Per-field fallback: an entry overriding only `streamIdleTimeoutMs` leaves the
connect leg at the lower levels. Configs without the keys behave
byte-identically (the standing uncapped-run rule). When a scoped override is
in effect the stall line names it (`idle window 1800s (role default
override)`), so a wide window never reads as a hang.

Slow-local-model recipe: a local endpoint that thinks minutes before the
first byte needs the IDLE leg widened, not the whole config. On the role
chain entry pinning the local endpoint set only `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2×`
its worst silent prefill stretch — every cloud provider in the same config
keeps the global watchdog untouched.

```yaml
roles:
  default:
    - provider: openai
      model: local-thinker
      baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
      streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000   # this entry only
  smol: [openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini]   # keeps 300s
```

- `lib/src/session_deadline.dart` — `SessionDeadline` (gh-1556): the ONE wall-clock budget source for a run — the temporal sibling of the FinalizeGate (gh-1412). Hosts inject `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms; resolved live per turn through the session-correlation seam above, so a mid-session `/timer` change reaches the next bash exec and the next LLM request); `fa --timer 25m` / `--deadline <duration|epoch>` (headless AND interactive) and the TUI `/timer` slash-command write the same single session value (env < flag < `/timer`; later wins). While armed, every LLM request context carries a per-turn `time-left: …` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at the ladder crossings (~50%, the T-3min wrap-up/background-job-drain steer, T-30s); the TUI status line renders a countdown chip as a pure projection. Missing/invalid env = feature off, byte-for-byte today's behavior; an explicit invalid user spec is a clear `FormatException`, never a silent wrong clock. Pure Dart — the clock is injected, no `dart:io` in `lib/`.
- `lib/src/env/memory_execution_env.dart` — `MemoryExecutionEnv`: pure-Dart in-memory `ExecutionEnv` (POSIX `/`-paths, default `Shell = UnavailableShell` reporting `shellUnavailable`). Default for tests and web consumers; shell-backed variants use `LocalShell` instead.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools for context hygiene. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` + `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree navigation). Summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` — **single source of truth** for post-run compaction. **never re-implement auto-compaction in the host**; add hooks to `AutoCompactorHooks`.

content.text:
37:- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
## Protocol tooling

- `lib/src/lsp/` — `lsp` tool (diagnostics/definition/references/rename): pure-Dart JSON-RPC over `LspTransport`; `.dart` → `dart language-server --protocol=lsp`; projects merge `.fah/lsp.json`. Lazy start, 5-min idle shutdown, crash respawn with backoff. Renames apply all-or-nothing through the env. IO via `lib/io.dart` + `builtinTools(env, lsp:)`. 1-indexed line/character; missing server = clean note, never a crash.
- `lib/src/mcp/` — MCP servers from `mcp:` section of `~/.fah/config.yaml` (strict `ConfigException` parsing). Stdio (`command`/`args`/`env`, NDJSON — **NOT** LSP's Content-Length) and remote (`url`, streamable-http default or legacy sse, `headers`). Message-level `McpTransport`; stdio framing pure Dart over `McpByteChannel` (process via `lib/io.dart`), HTTP transports pure Dart over injectable `package:http` (web gets remote; stdio = "not supported"). `McpManager` connects lazily in background, per-server `connecting`/`connected`/`failed` status, reconnect with capped backoff. Tools register as `mcp__<server>__<tool>` (exec tier, description prefixed with origin, inputSchema verbatim). Results map MCP blocks onto ours; `isError` throws; timeouts `mcp.toolCallTimeoutMs`.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Idle
  Idle --> Connecting: lazy, background
  Connecting --> Connected: handshake ok
  Connecting --> Failed: handshake fail
  Connected --> Connected: tool call
  Failed --> Reconnecting: backoff timer
  Reconnecting --> Connecting: retry
  Failed --> Failed: budget exhausted
  Connected --> Idle: 5 min idle
  note right of Failed: per-server status surfaced via onChanged
```

## Providers / models

See [providers.md](providers.md) for the full provider catalog.

Judge/smol model-class rule: the `smol` role also serves the structured
compaction hide judge — ONE call under a fixed attempt budget
(`compaction.judgeBudgetSeconds`, default 300 s) with a bounded input
(newest 512 ledger entries). Pick a class that answers within that budget
(a non-mandatory-reasoning class, or a budget sized to the class's
thinking time); a mandatory-reasoning class behind a queueing gateway can
make EVERY judge call hit the full budget. The engine defends itself: a
judge that times out falls back to the deterministic judge-less hide
after two consecutive failures, and the failure latches across runs —
auto-compact then skips the judge (deterministic hide) and pays one
probe call per window instead of the full budget per run. The named
failure line carries the attempt shape (input entries, est. tokens,
elapsed), so a slow-reasoning class reads differently from a wedged
endpoint in logs.

arguments.content:
### What changed
Auto-compact no longer re-pays the judge budget every run when the configured smol class cannot answer within it, and a judge timeout no longer kills the retry. Three engine changes in `lib/src/compaction/structured/`:

- **Per-call budget token**: the judge call runs under a child `CancelToken`; a timeout aborts only the in-flight call, while the retry and later LM stages keep the run-wide token live (`HideJudgeFn` gained an optional per-call token).
- **Cross-run judge-health latch** (`judge_health.dart`): consecutive judge failures persist as additive `structured_judge_health` custom records (newest wins, no migrations — old sessions load byte-identical). While latched, runs skip the judge (deterministic hide, receipt says "budget unwinnable for the configured class") and pay ONE probe per `judgeProbeAfter` window (default 10 min; a changed model class probes at once). Probe success unlatches; failure re-arms.
- **Timeout diagnosis**: the named #541 timeout line and the pass receipts now carry the attempt shape — input entries, est. tokens, elapsed (`judgeInputEntries`/`judgeInputTokens`/`judgeElapsedMs`/`judgeLatched`) — so a slow-reasoning class reads differently from a wedged endpoint in logs.

### Key decisions
- Health state rides `CustomRecord` — the established additive, context-invisible vehicle; owner directive honored (append-only, no migration rewrites; a fixture proves an old large session loads byte-identical).
- The latch threshold is the same count as the in-run #541 fallback (`judgeLatchAfter = 2`) — one state, no second knob.
- The probe tax is once per window, not per run; a changed `judgeTarget` bypasses the window because the latch is about the class, not the session.
- Docs: the smol/judge model-class rule (a class that answers within the budget, or a budget sized to the class) added to `docs/agents/providers.md`; CHANGELOG entry under `## Unreleased`.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/compaction/structured_judge_health_test.dart \
          test/compaction/structured_judge_fallback_test.dart \
          test/compaction/structured_engine_test.dart
```
New-code coverage: `judge_health.dart` 100% line coverage; no uncovered line inside the changed engine regions.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  RUN[auto-compact run] --> LOAD[load newest structured_judge_health record]
  LOAD -->|latched, probe window not due| SKIP[deterministic hide — no judge call]
  LOAD -->|latched, probe due / class changed| PROBE[ONE judge call on a per-call token]
  LOAD -->|fresh| JUDGE[one judge call on a per-call token]
  PROBE -->|success| UNLATCH[persist failures=0, run normally]
  PROBE -->|timeout / garbage| REARM[persist failures+1, deterministic hide]
  JUDGE -->|2 consecutive failures| LATCH[persist latch, deterministic hide]
  JUDGE -->|timeout| PERCALL[child token dies — retry + later stages stay live]
```

</details>
